previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: John, a homeless man with a history of hypertension and alcohol use disorder, was admitted with recurrent atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, likely triggered by heavy alcohol consumption and newly diagnosed multifocal pneumonia. He presented with tachycardia, left-sided chest pain, and a history of vomiting with blood. Initial management included IV diltiazem, which was insufficient for rate control, leading to the addition of metoprolol. Imaging revealed bilateral pleural effusions and multifocal lung opacities consistent with pneumonia, for which he was treated with intravenous antibiotics and transitioned to oral Augmentin. Abdominal pain was attributed to alcohol-induced mesenteritis, and elevated liver enzymes suggested alcoholic hepatitis. He received thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins for nutritional support and was monitored for alcohol withdrawal. By discharge, his symptoms had resolved, and he was stabilized on diltiazem, metoprolol, aspirin, omeprazole, and antibiotics. He was counseled extensively on alcohol cessation and discharged home with follow-up arranged for HIV testing, chest imaging, and primary care.

cause of his episodes and may result in death if he does not 
seek treatment for his heavy ETOH abuse.
